shorts_extract.hook: Changing one word in a question from 'contacted' to 'smashed' made witnesses see the same car crash 9 mph faster — and remember broken glass that never existed.
shorts_extract.core_experiment: Loftus & Palmer (1974): 45 + 150 witnesses, 5 verbs (31.8 to 40.8 mph), week-later phantom glass (32% vs 14%), plus 1995 'Lost in the Mall' (25% rich childhood false memories).
shorts_extract.twist: Memory is like a Wikipedia page editable on every recall, yet neutral immediate questioning preserves remarkably clean accuracy.
